title: Velouté Sauce
description: A classic French mother sauce prepared with a blond roux and white stock, creating a smooth, delicate sauce that serves as the foundation for many refined poultry, seafood, and veal sauces.

items: 500 ml (2 cups) hot white stock (chicken, veal, or fish)

instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Add the flour and whisk continuously for 3–4 minutes until a pale blond roux forms without browning deeply.
Gradually whisk in the hot white stock, adding a little at a time until smooth and lump-free.
Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer and cook for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally until lightly thickened.
Strain the sauce through a fine sieve or chinois for a silky finish.
Season lightly with salt and white pepper before serving.
chefTips: Use a high-quality homemade white stock for the best flavor.
Avoid over-browning the roux to preserve the sauce's light color.
Whisk continuously while adding stock to prevent lumps.
Velouté is the base for Suprême, Allemande, and Normande sauces.
Perfect with poultry, seafood, veal, and other delicate white meats.
